correctness.rationale: An exact strip-intersection enumeration gives precisely six extreme points ±(1,1/2), ±(-1,2/3), ±(1/7,8/7) of H, hence the original displayed K=T H (T=diag(2,1)) is a genuine centrally symmetric hexagon. The unit disk is the John ellipse of H because all three strip normals are unit and positive opposite-symmetrized contact weights (11/16,125/224,169/224) sum to isotropic identity. Exact Q0=(1/65)[[49,4],[4,48]] is SPD, includes all six vertices with equality, and positive vertex weights (6929/12264,12375/16352,4753/7008) satisfy sum b_i v_i v_i^T=Q0^{-1}; the dual John contact criterion certifies it is the Löwner ellipse. Independent exact rational checks verified both certificates, all vertices, and detQ0=2336/4225. After T the endpoint matrices are diag(1/4,1) and (1/65)[[49/4,2],[2,48]] and their commutator has (1,2) entry -3/130. Bochi Theorem1.2 proves the unique fixed-area maximal-intersection ellipse varies continuously from John to Löwner in the full stated area interval, so a pair of strictly interior parameters near opposite endpoints still has noncommuting matrices. A centered ellipse family with a common orthogonal principal-axis basis would require pairwise commuting Q. Every centrally symmetric polygon with <6 vertices is an affine image of a square; uniqueness and quarter-turn symmetry force disks for the square and a homothetic axis-fixed family for any parallelogram. Thus 6 is minimal.
residual_risks: No formula for the entire intermediate MI path or monotone angular rotation is proved; only existence of two noncoaxial strictly interior areas. Bochi interpolation requires a centrally symmetric full-dimensional planar body, satisfied here.
